**Opening argument for c = 1/25**

**Step 1: The reduced graph is triangle-free.** Take a regularity partition with clusters X, Y, Z forming a triangle in the reduced graph. Since α(G) = o(n), X contains an edge x₁x₂. Regularity gives Ω(n) common neighbours of x₁ and x₂ in Y, which contain an edge y₁y₂. Regularity again gives a common neighbour z₁ of all four in Z, producing a K₅. So any K₅-free G with α = o(n) has a triangle-free reduced graph, and within-cluster edges are o(n²).

**Step 2: Lower bound.** Take the balanced blow-up of C₅ with sparse triangle-free graphs inside parts. This is K₅-free, has α = o(n), and has n²/5 edges. Its maximum cut keeps 4 of the 5 part-pairs. The cut objective is multilinear in the part fractions, so splitting parts doesn't help. This forces n²/25 deletions, so c ≥ 1/25.

**Step 3: Upper bound.** Cut the reduced graph optimally and delete the within-cluster edges. The problem becomes maximising, over triangle-free weighted graphs, the minimum weight of edges left monochromatic. For C₅, AM–GM gives at most 1/25, with equality at uniform weights. Other triangle-free candidates I checked (C₇, Petersen, Andrásfai graphs, a 6-vertex C₅ extension) do not exceed 1/25.

**Step 4:** Any answer above 1/25 needs a structure the triangle lemma excludes, so B's 1/8 is not supported.

I should be upfront that Step 3 rests on checking candidate graphs rather than a complete proof that no triangle-free weighted graph beats C₅.
